facts.title: Accelerating GPU Inference of Large Language Models with Moderately Unstructured Sparse Weight Matrices
facts.event_hint: DAC 2026 paper proposing sparse matrix inference acceleration for LLMs on GPUs
facts.problem: At moderate unstructured sparsity (~50%), existing GPU kernels for sparse matrix multiplication (SpMM) cannot outperform dense counterparts, limiting inference acceleration while maintaining model quality.
facts.mechanism: Three-layer matrix storage format: (i) Sparse-TC layer enabling sparse tensor cores to accelerate SpMM; (ii) Slot-Filling layer using parallel differential distance (PDD) encoding for matrix compression with low-cost on-chip decoding; (iii) lightweight Residual Layer (CSR format) for remaining non-zeros. Co-optimized SpMM kernel jointly utilizes sparse tensor cores and CUDA cores with pipelined execution overlapping computation with memory access.

evidence.claim: Kernel achieves up to 1.64× speedup over SpInfer at 50% sparsity
Kernel achieves up to 1.81× speedup over FlashLLM at 50% sparsity
End-to-end inference throughput up to 41.4% higher than FlashLLM for OPT-30B
Peak memory usage reduced by 21.4% compared to dense baseline
Format conversion cost is one-time: 41.1s for OPT-30B, 92.6s for OPT-66B

facts.evaluation_context: NVIDIA H100 SXM5 GPUs with 80GB HBM3, NVLink interconnect; OPT-30B and OPT-66B models pruned with Wanda algorithm; batch sizes 8/16/32; sparsity levels 50%/60%/70%; input/output sequence length 512; GCC 12.3.0 and NVCC 12.6.
facts.limitations: Does not outperform FlashLLM under high sparsity due to zero-padding requirements; constrained during compute-bound prefill phase with large N (runs slower than cuBLAS); targets decoding phase optimization; requires GPUs with sparse tensor cores and HBM; incurs slightly higher memory usage than SpInfer due to bitmap encoding in baseline method. Absolute throughput in tokens/second or latency in milliseconds not reported. HBM bandwidth utilization or memory traffic measurements not provided. Power consumption or performance-per-watt not measured. Supplement contains only acknowledgments and references—no additional experimental data addressing evidence gaps.
facts.project_relevance: Addresses GPU memory bandwidth bottleneck in LLM inference through sparse matrix computation co-design with modern GPU hardware (sparse tensor cores + HBM). Relevant to direction on AI accelerator memory interface and hardware-software co-design. Demonstrates 1.64× kernel speedup and 21.4% memory reduction at 50% sparsity on H100, showing how algorithm-hardware specialization can extract performance from memory-bound workloads. However, absolute throughput numbers (tokens/second), HBM bandwidth utilization measurements, and power efficiency metrics are not reported—key evidence gaps for assessing real-world deployment value.

evidence_gaps.question: What is the absolute throughput in tokens/second or latency in milliseconds for OPT-30B and OPT-66B at batch sizes 8/16/32?
What are the specific HBM bandwidth utilization numbers or memory traffic measurements?
What is the power consumption or performance-per-watt compared to dense baselines?

facts.title: GPUSparse: GPU-Accelerated Learned Sparse Retrieval with Parallel Inverted Indices
facts.event_hint: arXiv paper published 2026-06-24 on GPU-accelerated exact learned sparse retrieval using parallel inverted indices
facts.problem: Learned sparse retrieval models (SPLADE) achieve quality competitive with dense models while preserving interpretability, but inference-time scoring relies on CPU-bound inverted index traversal algorithms (WAND, Block-Max WAND). This creates a fundamental bottleneck for real-time serving at scale. Existing GPU sparse retrieval systems (Seismic) trade 25% recall for speed.
facts.mechanism: GPUSparse introduces: (1) GPU-parallel inverted index with block-aligned, warp-coalesced posting lists, (2) batched scatter-add scoring algorithm processing hundreds of queries simultaneously, (3) fused Triton kernels. The scatter-add kernel processes only O(q_bar * L_bar) entries per query (query terms × posting lists). A document-parallel kernel trades work-efficiency for bandwidth utilization.

evidence.claim: 235x speedup over Pyserini CPU exact scoring at 8.8M documents
evidence.condition: MS MARCO passage ranking 8.8M passages, batch 500, H100 80GB

evidence.claim: Achieves 787 QPS throughput at 8.8M documents with batch 500
evidence.condition: MS MARCO 8.8M passages, batch 500, H100 80GB, exact scoring

evidence.claim: Document-parallel kernel achieves 62.6% of H100 peak HBM bandwidth
Scatter-add kernel achieves 12.5 GB/s effective bandwidth (0.37% of peak) due to scattered atomic writes
8.5 GB for inverted index at 8.8M passages (11% of 80GB H100)

facts.evaluation_context: Evaluated on MS MARCO passage ranking (8.8M passages) with real SPLADE embeddings. Hardware: H100 80GB GPU. Metrics include MRR@10, Recall@1000, per-query latency, QPS throughput. Cross-domain validation on BEIR benchmarks (SciFact, NFCorpus, TREC-COVID). Comparison against Pyserini CPU exact scoring, Seismic (fastest CPU sparse), cuSPARSE SpMV, and dense matmul ground truth.
facts.limitations: GPU cost: H100 GPU is substantially more expensive than CPU-only retrieval. Single-query latency 9.6ms at 8.8M docs - CPU methods faster for single-query approximate search. Score buffer memory scales as O(B*N): 44GB at batch 500 with 8.8M docs (55% of H100). No dynamic updates without full index rebuild. 6x slower than Seismic for approximate top-10 retrieval at 8.8M.
facts.project_relevance: GPUSparse demonstrates memory-bandwidth-bound sparse retrieval on H100 with 62.6% peak utilization achieved via document-parallel kernel. The work-efficiency vs bandwidth-efficiency tradeoff is fundamental: scatter-add processes only query-relevant postings (work-efficient) at 0.37% bandwidth utilization, while doc-parallel achieves 62.6% peak but reads 76GB vs 0.09GB per batch. The 8.5GB index size at 8.8M passages shows sparse format memory advantage vs dense (~1TB). Index cannot be updated without full rebuild - limitation for dynamic workloads.

facts.title: REMOP: REmote-Memory-aware OPerator Optimization
facts.event_hint: REMOP framework for remote-memory-aware database operator optimization
facts.problem: Classical disk-spilling operator heuristics minimize I/O volume but can trigger excessive transfer rounds under remote memory where each round incurs fixed RTT, making total latency sensitive to round count
facts.mechanism: Transfer-round-aware intra-operator buffer partitioning strategies; derives operator-specific input/output buffer splits for blocked nested-loop join, external merge sort, and external hash join to minimize total latency L = D/BW + C*RTT

evidence.claim: REMOP reduces transfer rounds by up to 97% and operator runtime by up to 48% on spill-heavy microbenchmarks
evidence.condition: BNLJ single-operator query, selectivity f=1/256K, memory budget M=4K pages, two-node compute-memory testbed

evidence.claim: REMOP reduces BNLJ runtime by 48.7% and transfer rounds by 97.1% at L-optimal buffer settings
evidence.condition: BNLJ with (rin=0.4, pR=0.6), selectivity f=1/256K, M=4K pages

evidence.claim: REMOP lowers average runtime of spilling TPC-H queries by 22.7%
evidence.condition: TPC-H spilling queries, two-node compute-memory testbed

evidence.claim: REMOP lowers average runtime of spilling TPC-DS queries by 26.4%
evidence.condition: TPC-DS spilling queries, two-node compute-memory testbed

evidence.claim: REMOP achieves gains up to 51% under higher remote-memory latency

facts.evaluation_context: Two-node compute-memory testbed; DuckDB implementation; TCP-based REMON and RDMA-based Infiniswap backends evaluated; microbenchmarks for BNLJ, EMS, EHJ; end-to-end TPC-H and TPC-DS spilling queries
facts.limitations: Testbed evaluation only; no production deployment data; RDMA backend (Infiniswap) shows software overhead and page-granularity mismatch that can diminish raw RDMA advantage; model assumes fixed budget M and does not address dynamic memory redistribution across concurrent queries; RTT parameter tau proportional to BW*RTT must be estimated for deployment
facts.project_relevance: Topic alignment strong (内存语义、DSA卸载: remote memory/disaggregated memory semantics). REMOP addresses memory resource semantics by exposing transfer-round cost structure of remote memory swapping—directly addressing how memory tier changes latency characteristics. Demonstrates端到端收益传导: operator-level microbenchmark gains (48% runtime reduction, 97% transfer-round reduction) propagate to TPC-H (22.7%) and TPC-DS (26.4%) query-level improvements. No DSA/IAA offload focus, but quantifies CPU/data-movement cost of remote memory semantics through RTT-dominated cost model.
